steps.say: Myelopathy means the spinal cord itself is diseased, and the first question is whether compression is causing it. Compression from disc, tumour, pus or blood needs urgent surgery, while inflammation, B twelve deficiency and ischaemia are treated medically. A sensory level on the trunk marks the cord segment involved, and missing compression is the commonest serious error.
steps.tx: **Myelopathy** is cord dysfunction, and the first split is **compressive** versus **noncompressive**. Compression by disc, tumour, epidural abscess or haematoma needs urgent **surgical decompression**. Inflammation, **vitamin B12** deficiency, copper deficiency and ischaemia are medical. A truncal **sensory level** marks the segment, and back pain with fever suggests **Pott spine**.

steps.say: Cord compression announces itself with back pain, weak legs and a sensory level that rises as it worsens. Bladder retention with brisk reflexes points to the cord rather than the roots. M R I of the whole spine is the first test, and it is done as an emergency because deficits become permanent after hours of compression. Never wait for morning when the legs are failing.
steps.tx: **Cord compression** presents with back pain, leg weakness and a rising **sensory level**. **Urinary retention** with brisk reflexes points to cord, not roots. **MRI whole spine** is the first test and is done as an emergency. **Dexamethasone** is given while awaiting surgery. Deficits complete beyond a **day** rarely recover fully.

steps.say: Transverse myelitis inflames the cord across its width and leaves a T two bright lesion with swelling. Infection, M S and N M O are the mimics to exclude, and spinal fluid with oligoclonal bands with M R I brain separates them. Steroids in high doses are the first treatment, and plasma exchange rescues severe cases that do not respond. Most patients are left with some disability.
steps.tx: **Transverse myelitis** gives a bilateral sensorimotor level with **T2 hyperintensity** and cord swelling. **MS**, **NMO** and infection are excluded with brain MRI and **CSF oligoclonal bands**. **Methylprednisolone** 1 g daily for 3 to 5 days is first line. **Plasma exchange** rescues severe or steroid unresponsive cases.

steps.say: N M O spectrum disorder attacks optic nerves and cord together and leaves longitudinally extensive lesions of three or more segments. Aquaporin four antibody confirms it, and M O G antibody marks its closest mimic. Attacks are severe and recovery is poor, so prevention with targeted immunotherapy matters more than acute treatment. Both antibodies are tested in every longitudinally extensive myelitis.
steps.tx: **NMO spectrum disorder** causes **longitudinally extensive** lesions of 3 or more segments with **aquaporin 4** antibody positivity. **Optic neuritis** with myelitis is the classic pairing. Attacks are severe with poor recovery, so **relapse prevention** with targeted immunotherapy matters most. **MOG antibody** disease mimics it but recovers better.

points: 3 or more segments, AQP4 positive, poor recovery
left.title: NMO spectrum

points: Often shorter lesions, MOG positive, better recovery
right.title: MOGAD myelitis

steps.say: B twelve deficiency melts the posterior and lateral columns together and is called subacute combined degeneration. Nitrous oxide abuse causes the same picture in young people by inactivating B twelve. Copper deficiency copies it exactly, so copper is checked when B twelve is normal. Tingling feet with lost vibration sense and large red cells are the bedside clues, and replacement stops progression.
steps.tx: **Subacute combined degeneration** from **vitamin B12** deficiency hits posterior plus lateral columns. **Nitrous oxide** abuse causes it in the young. **Copper deficiency** copies it exactly, so copper is checked when B12 is normal. Lost **vibration sense** with tingling feet and macrocytosis are clues. **Replacement** halts it; delay leaves permanent deficit.

steps.say: Spinal cord infarct follows aortic surgery or severe hypotension and hits the anterior cord first. Burning back pain with sudden paraplegia with lost pain sensation but spared vibration sense is the signature, because the posterior columns are fed separately. Diffusion M R I shows the infarct, and spinal angiography finds a fistula when the course is slow and stepwise. Time is cord, as in brain.
steps.tx: **Anterior spinal artery infarct** follows aortic surgery or hypotension. Sudden paraplegia with **dissociated sensory loss** (pain lost, vibration spared) is the signature. **Diffusion MRI** confirms infarct. A **dural arteriovenous fistula** causes slow stepwise paraparesis with cord oedema and flow voids, cured by **embolisation**.

steps.say: T B of the spine destroys the disc with the two adjacent vertebrae and collects a cold abscess that compresses the cord. Most patients have pulmonary T B or contact history, and E S R with Mantoux supports the diagnosis. Biopsy with GeneXpert confirms it, and treatment runs antitubercular drugs for many months with bracing. Surgery is reserved for compression, instability and deformity.
steps.tx: **Pott spine** destroys disc plus adjacent vertebrae with paraspinal **cold abscess**. Back pain with kyphosis and constitutional symptoms is typical. **GeneXpert** on biopsy confirms TB. **Antitubercular therapy** runs 12 months or more with bracing. **Surgery** is for cord compression, instability and progressive deformity.

steps.say: Every myelopathy is worked up in the same order, and the order itself is examined. Whole spine M R I with contrast comes first to rule out compression. Spinal fluid with oligoclonal bands comes next when M R I shows inflammation. Aquaporin four with M O G antibodies follows when the lesion is long, and B twelve with copper with syphilis testing closes the list. This sequence misses nothing treatable.
steps.tx: **Workup order** is fixed: **MRI whole spine** with contrast first, then **CSF** with oligoclonal bands if inflammatory. **AQP4 and MOG antibodies** follow for long lesions, then **B12, copper and syphilis** testing. **CT chest** hunts sarcoid and malignancy. Skipping straight to steroids without MRI risks missing a **compressible** lesion.

steps.say: Compressive lesions are decompressed urgently, and steroids are given on the way to theatre. Steroids with plasma exchange treat inflammatory myelitis, and immunotherapy prevents N M O relapses. B twelve with copper replacement reverses metabolic disease when started early. Fistulas are embolised, and abscesses are drained with antibiotics. Rehabilitation with bladder care decides the final quality of life.
steps.tx: **Decompression** within hours saves compressive myelopathy; **dexamethasone** bridges to theatre. **Methylprednisolone** with **plasma exchange** treats inflammatory myelitis. **Immunotherapy** prevents NMO relapses. **B12 and copper** replacement reverses metabolic disease early. **Embolisation** cures fistula, and **bladder care** with physiotherapy decides long term function.

steps.say: A missed compressive lesion ends in permanent paraplegia with pressure injuries and sepsis, which is why speed is the whole game. Inflammatory myelitis often leaves bladder symptoms with erectile dysfunction and chronic pain. N M O relapses accumulate blindness with paraplegia, so prevention is lifelong. Even treated Pott spine can leave kyphosis that compresses the cord years later.
steps.tx: **Complications** decide outcome: pressure injuries, **urosepsis** and contractures follow permanent paraplegia. **Neurogenic bladder** with retention needs timed catheterisation. **NMO** relapses accumulate deficits, so prevention never stops. Healed **Pott spine** can kyphose and compress late. Depression with unemployment is common and needs addressing.

steps.say: For the exam, lock in compression first with emergency M R I, three segments for N M O, aquaporin four antibody, posterior plus lateral columns for B twelve, and dissociated loss for anterior spinal infarct. Doses are small numbers, so memorise the six to ten facts in this table exactly as written and match each antibody with its disease.
steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** exclude **compression** first with emergency MRI. **3 or more segments** with **aquaporin 4** positivity marks NMO. Posterior plus lateral columns mark **B12** deficiency. Dissociated loss marks **anterior spinal** infarct. Methylprednisolone 1 g for 3 to 5 days treats transverse myelitis, and GeneXpert confirms Pott spine.
